er: Draw an ER diagram for a library system: books, authors (many-to-many with books), members, loans, reservations, branches, and the copies of books that each branch holds. Show primary and foreign keys.
er-clinic: Draw an ER diagram for a veterinary clinic: owners, pets (each pet has one owner), vets, appointments between a pet and a vet, treatments given at an appointment, medications (many-to-many with treatments, with the dose), and invoices for appointments. Show primary and foreign keys.
er-shop: Draw an ER diagram for an online shop: customers, addresses, orders, order items, products, categories (a category can have a parent category), suppliers, reviews and payments. Show primary and foreign keys.
class: Draw a UML class diagram for an e-commerce domain: Customer, Address, Order, OrderLine, Product, Category, an abstract Payment with CreditCardPayment and PayPalPayment subclasses, and Shipment. Show attributes, key methods and multiplicities.
swimlane: Draw a flowchart with swimlanes for Customer, Web Shop, Payment Provider and Warehouse for an online order: the customer places the order, the shop checks stock (decision: in stock? if not, notify the customer and end), the payment is authorized (decision: approved? if not, retry up to 3 times, then cancel the order), the warehouse picks, packs and ships, and the customer receives the shipping confirmation.
aws: Draw an AWS architecture diagram for a web shop: users reach CloudFront and an Application Load Balancer; inside a VPC with two availability zones, an ECS Fargate service for the API in private subnets, an RDS PostgreSQL primary with a standby replica, and ElastiCache Redis; static assets in S3; orders go to an SQS queue processed by a Lambda function that sends emails through SES. Use the official AWS icons.
sequence: Draw a sequence diagram of the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE between User, Browser SPA, Authorization Server and Resource API, including the token refresh when the access token has expired.
